questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13987450/assets/7dc806c646f1e9f5edbfef789fbdc9dfca2745c637906bd61eccb8072440e8c0.png)

In square units rounded to one decimal place, find the area of $△ABC$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={63}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘}) & =\frac{3x+2}{3x} \\ 3x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘}) & =3x+2 \\ 3x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-3x & =2 \\ 3x(\operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-1) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{3(\operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-1)} \\ x & =0.692\,5…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x+2=3(0.692\,5…)+2=4.077\,6…, \\ AC & =3x=3(0.692\,5…)=2.077\,6….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(2.077\,6…)(4.077\,6…) \\  & =4.236\,0… \\  & ≈4.2,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the one decimal place.

Find the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={45}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({45}^{∘}) & =\frac{5x+5}{6x} \\ 1 & =\frac{5x+5}{6x} \\ 6x & =5x+5 \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =6x=6(5)=30, \\ BC & =5x+5=5(5)+5=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 30\cdot 30 \\  & =450.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13987450/assets/f1880dc62f774152ce5076a313928c0e8109ca174184704c5880891ed9243718.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{5}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{2}{5} & =\frac{2x+4}{6x+8} \\ 2(6x+8) & =5(2x+4) \\ 12x+16 & =10x+20 \\ 12x-10x & =20-16 \\ 2x & =4 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x+4=2(2)+4=8, \\ AC & =6x+8=6(2)+8=20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 20\cdot 8 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13987450/assets/4572bd2ef8f6086ed80f5ac21e045e3cf2359680872a958a40d2f1e72f22d980.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=2,$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=2.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ 2 & =\frac{9x+2}{5x-1} \\ 2(5x-1) & =9x+2 \\ 10x-2 & =9x+2 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =9x+2=9(4)+2=38, \\ AC & =5x-1=5(4)-1=19.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 38\cdot 19 \\  & =361.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Area of a Triangle Given a Trigonometric Ratio of an Angle and the Length of a Leg
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13987450/assets/ba89c2cf139dd6251804ed0758c4edc4690463ba5ae14867549881a29736f9e6.png)

Given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{12}{13},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{12}{13},$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the cosine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{12}{13} & =\frac{12}{AB} \\ AB & =\frac{12}{12}\cdot 13 \\ AB & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the missing side $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{13}^{2}-{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169-144} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 12 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$
